summary: Cromwell (Skunk Island) tower in Carlton County; a 1949 Aermotor build per Forest Lookouts; a 1952 survey gives about 80 ft, not 100; listed standing.

facts.design: Aermotor tower; four-legged steel structure with an enclosed observation platform at the top

events.note: A 100-foot Aermotor tower was erected (Forest Lookouts build line)
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description gives the tower as approximately 80 feet high

evidence.supports: also called the Skunk Island lookout tower
described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1952
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1952
THE STATION IS LOCATED ABOUT 3-3/4 MILES NORTHEAST OF CROMWELL.

evidence.supports: four-legged steel structure about 80 feet high
evidence.quote: IT IS A 4 LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE, APPROXIMATELY 80 FEET

evidence.supports: enclosed observation platform at the top
evidence.quote: HIGH AND WITH AN ENCLOSED OBSERVATION PLATFORM AT THE TOP.

evidence.supports: listed as a standing tower in Carlton County
placed within the Fond du Lac State Forest
Wikidata image of the tower on Wikimedia Commons

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not settled. The 1949 build line gives 100 feet (30.5 m); the 1952 Coast and Geodetic Survey description gives approximately 80 feet (about 24 m). The record keeps 30.5 m; an editor should decide which figure to show.

sources.title: Cromwell (Skunk Island) - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (centraluslookouts.weebly.com), reproducing a Coast and Geodetic Survey station description

notes_for_editor: The Forest Lookouts page is the only source for the 1949 build. A search summary claimed a 1935 CCC build; the cached page says 1949 and does not mention the CCC or 1935, so 1935 was not used. Height conflict: 100 ft (1949 build line) against approximately 80 ft (1952 survey); the brief's 30.5 m matches the 100-ft figure and was kept, so the editor should choose. The Wikidata elevation of 1,394 ft matches the brief's 424.9 m. No National Historic Lookout Register page was found in the cache (one guessed URL returned 404). No staffing, notable fires, access or current condition were found. The Commons photo is listed on Wikidata but its file page was not read, so it is not added to photos.
